An authorized caller receives the requested page review and cross-room access is denied.
A valid session can be renewed and missing or malformed sessions are rejected.
A valid session initializes, commits a public scene operation, and the committed state survives restart and later join.

A valid scene create operation is acknowledged and becomes visible to another public client.
A start event creates one in-progress command and is not duplicated when updates arrive.
An append update preserves prior points and reaches observers in order.
A stop event commits the final points and the command is complete in a later snapshot.
The legacy undo event hides the addressed command and returns a committed acknowledgement.
The legacy redo event restores the addressed command and returns a committed acknowledgement.
Delete removes the addressed command and leaves unrelated commands unchanged.
A batch move updates all requested elements atomically and preserves non-target elements.
A batch update applies the requested fields to all and only the selected commands.
A batch stop commits every command exactly once and preserves ordering.
Adding a page commits a new page and page-specific content remains isolated after navigation.
A cursor update is visible to peers with server-trusted identity and does not mutate scene state.
A leaving cursor is removed for peers without changing persistent scene state.
Selection bounds are broadcast to peers but are not persisted as scene mutations.
The requester receives the current online member set and no unrelated room members.
A create operation produces exactly the declared element on the declared page and is replayable.
An append adds only the declared source range and replay does not duplicate points.
A transform applies the declared matrix to all targets and leaves other elements unchanged.
A style patch changes only declared style fields on addressed elements.
Erase intervals remove only the targeted stroke fragments and survive replay.
Delete removes all and only the listed elements, including after snapshot replay.
Insert and delete patches preserve grapheme order and converge across clients.
Undo hides only the target client's stroke on both visible canvases; redo restores it while the other client's stroke remains visible.
Clear removes content only up to the declared order key on the selected page.
The gateway accepts a valid create payload and rejects a missing descriptor.
The gateway accepts valid appended points and rejects an invalid source index or point payload.
The gateway accepts a non-singular transform target and rejects an empty target list.
The gateway accepts a valid style patch and rejects an empty style patch.
The gateway accepts valid erase intervals and rejects an empty target list.
The gateway accepts valid delete targets and rejects an empty target list.
The gateway accepts a valid grapheme insertion and rejects an empty patch list.
The gateway accepts a valid history toggle and rejects a missing history group ID.
The gateway accepts a valid clear watermark and rejects a malformed ordering key.
The home route exposes working room creation and join flows with user-visible validation.
The invite route displays the resolved room, handles invalid or expired tokens, and joins the intended room.
The authorized room route renders the expected room state; missing-session and missing-room paths must not display stale canvas content.
Cursor selection targets the expected element without creating or mutating scene content.
Pointer input creates a visible stroke locally and a second participant observes it in the expected region.
Pencil input renders and persists a stroke with its declared opacity behavior.
Highlighter input preserves the declared transparency and remains consistent across participants.
Path erasing removes only hit stroke fragments and is reversible through history.
Object erasing removes the hit object and preserves unrelated objects.
Line input creates the expected endpoints, style, and remote result.
Arrow input creates the expected direction, bounds, and remote result.
Rectangle input creates the expected bounds and fill or outline semantics.
Rounded rectangle input preserves the rounded shape and expected bounds.
Ellipse input creates the expected bounds and remains correctly hit-testable.
Text input commits Unicode graphemes and formatting through the public editor flow.
Sticky-note input commits editable text and its expected background and style.
Sticker input handles a successful asset and a missing or failed asset without corrupting the scene.
